title: Uniformly bounded derived towers with pro-zero cohomology are pro-zero
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ and cohomology functors $H^q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $X_n\in D(\mathcal A)$ for $n\geq1$ and let $t_{k,n}:X_k\to X_n$ for $k\geq n$ satisfy $t_{n,n}=\mathrm{id}$ and $t_{\ell,n}=t_{k,n}\circ t_{\ell,k}$ for $\ell\geq k\geq n$. Suppose there are fixed integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^q(X_n)=0$ for every $n$ and every $q\notin[a,b]$. Suppose also that for each integer $q$ and each $n\geq1$ there exists $k\geq n$ with $H^q(t_{k,n})=0$. Then for each $n\geq1$ there exists $k\geq n$ with $t_{k,n}=0$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.

source.place: Tag 0G3B (lemma-essentially-constant-cohomology), specialization to essentially constant cohomology systems with value zero

proof.text: Induct on the natural number (b-a).toNat. In the base case a=b, the vanishing assumptions give IsGE a and IsLE a for every object. By the single-degree identification, source and target are isomorphic to singleFunctor a objects. This functor is full, and its composite with degree-a homology is naturally isomorphic to the identity, hence faithful. Conjugate any transition with zero degree-a homology by these isomorphisms; fullness and faithfulness show it is zero. Apply the pro-zero hypothesis in degree a at each target index.

When a<b, apply the functorial truncation triangle at a to X, obtaining a functor from the opposite natural-number category to distinguished triangles. The upper tower Y=truncGE(a+1)(X) has cohomology in [a+1,b]. To transfer pro-zero homology to Y, use the long exact sequence: H^q(X) to H^q(Y) is epic for q>a, because H^(q+1)(truncLE a X)=0. Naturality and cancellation of this epimorphism show that any transition killed on H^q(X) is killed on H^q(Y). For q<a+1, H^q(Y)=0 already. Similarly H^a(truncLE a X) to H^a(X) is monic, because H^(a-1)(Y)=0; naturality transfers degree-a zero maps to the lower tower.

source.place: Tag 0G3B proof, functorial canonical truncation triangle and its cohomology sequence

proof.text: Apply the induction hypothesis to the upper tower Y, since (b-(a+1)).toNat is one smaller. Each lower truncation is concentrated in degree a, since truncLE preserves the lower bound a; the single-degree argument and the degree-a hypothesis make its tower pro-zero. At a fixed target n, choose m>=n killing the lower transition and k>=n killing the upper transition. The transitions from max(m,k) to n factor through the chosen zero transitions by the functor laws, so both outer transitions vanish simultaneously. Apply the pro-zero-middle lemma for this tower of distinguished triangles; its middle transition is exactly the transition of X.
